thread:
Dev Patel: pulling together top customer asks re: model change transparency + examples of where we’ve burned folks during rollouts. want this in one place before we go bug platform/console again.

Dev Patel: quick bullets from last ~2 weeks:
- “tell me what changed” when a model version shifts under an alias (customers see behavior drift, can’t explain to their stakeholders)
- need a customer-visible changelog w/ dates + impact (not random Slack/DMs)
- machine-readable feed (RSS/JSON) so they can pipe into change-management
- version pinning confidence: “if i pin, i should be able to *prove* what i ran” (support wants this too)
- deprecation timelines + replacement guidance (60–90d heads up, not day-of)

Dev Patel: examples of confusion (support escalations):
1) customer pinned `model=redwood-chat` (alias) thinking it was stable; rollout updated default behind it; they thought we changed their prompt/infra
2) “same version” but output drift after we changed runtime/kernel/quantization profile (we didn’t communicate it as a model change)
3) dedicated customer: rollout moved them from region A -> region B during capacity event; latency changed and they assumed model changed

Dev Patel: Owen can you add your greatest hits from escalations? Paula/Marissa/Elliot if you have specific phrasing customers used, drop it here.

Owen Phillips: yep. 2 big patterns:
- “we need an audit trail.” esp enterprise: who approved change, when it was published, immutable history. they don’t care if it’s “just metadata,” they treat it like a production dependency.
- “we need to diff versions.” even if it’s not full eval diff, they want *some* structured fields: context window, tool calling support, safety/policy notes, deprecation status.

Owen Phillips: actual customer language from last escalation (paraphrased): “My VP asked what changed. I have nothing to show besides ‘trust us’.” :grimacing:

Owen Phillips: also: customers keep asking “what is the canonical version id?” because they see:
- docs say one thing
- console shows model name
- API returns `model=` but not always the resolved version

Owen Phillips: would help if every response included something like `resolved_model_version` + a link to the entry.

Marissa Cole: +1. for product framing: i keep hearing two jobs-to-be-done:
1) during incident/behavior change: “help me *identify* what changed fast”
2) for governance: “help me *approve/track* changes proactively”

Marissa Cole: can we list top 5 “required fields” customers want in the changelog entry? not internal schema, just customer-safe.

Paula Mendes: from rollouts POV, customers ask for:
- “effective date/time” of change (and region) + when it hit their traffic
- compatibility notes (tool calling / JSON mode / max context)
- rollback guidance: “if this breaks me, what do i pin to?”

Paula Mendes: we also need to be explicit about when a rollout is:
- new version available (opt-in)
vs
- default alias moved (opt-out)

Paula Mendes: that ambiguity is where they get upset.

Elliot Price: for docs wording: customers respond well to “what’s the impact” sections:
- behavior/quality: we can’t always quantify, but we can say “no expected output change” vs “minor output change possible” (careful)
- perf/latency: “expected lower latency” etc
- compatibility: “tool calling now supported” etc
- action required: “none” / “pin to X” / “update config”

Elliot Price: also strong ask: “don’t bury this in a PDF.” they want a stable URL per version + feed.

Wei Chen: +1 and please no internal names/vendor specifics in public notes. customers don’t need “we swapped kernel XYZ” — they need “perf improvement for long contexts” + any constraints.

Connor O'Brien: from release eng angle, the confusion in (2) is real: runtime release trains can change throughput/behavior for a subset of models.

Connor O'Brien: customers don’t care *why* (runtime vs model change) — they just want a single place to look. if we can cross-link “runtime release impacted these model versions” that would reduce back-and-forth.

Talia Benson: i’m capturing this for the project intake. proposed “customer-required” changelog fields (draft):
- model name + explicit version id
- release date + “available in” (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) + regions if relevant
- change type taxonomy: perf / bugfix / compatibility / deprecation / policy
- impact summary (customer-safe)
- compatibility + limits (context window, tool calling, structured output)
- deprecation timeline + replacement (if applicable)
- link(s): docs page, console, status of rollout

Talia Benson: anything missing?

Owen Phillips: add “supportability” note: known issues + workaround. even a short line helps support deflect tickets.

Dev Patel: +1. even “Known issue: function calling may fail at high concurrency; workaround: retry / lower parallelism” is gold.

Marissa Cole: for MVP, i’d rather we require less but always have it present. empty sections create distrust (“why is compatibility blank?”).

Paula Mendes: also: customers want to filter by “only changes that could affect output.” they don’t want noise.

Elliot Price: docs can support a short “No customer-visible changes” entry type but we should use sparingly.

Connor O'Brien: +1, otherwise people ignore the feed.

Dev Patel: ok summary i’ll send to platform/console:
- must-have: canonical version id, resolved version in API, stable URL per version
- must-have: customer-safe impact + compatibility notes always present
- want: RSS/JSON feed + export (for change-management)
- enterprise: immutable history + approver/audit trail
- reduce confusion: one source of truth, runtime changes cross-linked

Dev Patel: thanks all. i’ll link this thread in the intake + ping Dylan/Chloe when i have it cleaned up. :thumbsup:

Elliot Price: pls tag docs early when templates land — we can provide a style lint checklist.

Paula Mendes: and tag me on the alias vs pinned UX copy; we need that crystal clear.

Owen Phillips: i’ll pull 2–3 anonymized customer quotes and paste here later today.

Dev Patel: perfect.
